main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking sambal belacan (smelly food) in the shared kitchen, given its effect on the flat, and what rules should apply.

A-B.evidence: Both object to the smell, but B wants only a warning (T14, T25) while A says a warning doesn't help the living room (T20) and pushes for Saturday cooking (T22, T24).

A-C.evidence: Both are bothered by the smell; C says a warning doesn't help the laundry (T9), A wants no strong-smelling cooking (T1, T11). They never address each other directly.

A-D.evidence: D resisted a ban (T4, T10, T12), then offered once a week (T21); A said that is better and proposed Saturday (T22). D has not accepted Saturday (T23).

B-C.evidence: C says a warning doesn't help the laundry (T9) and 'It's the same smell' (T17), while B calls laundry a different problem (T16) and keeps asking only for a warning (T18).

B-D.evidence: B repeatedly asks D for a warning (T8, T14, T18). D asks about the house rule (T19) and offers once a week (T21), then asks what works for B (T23). B says a warning is all he needs (T25). D has not yet agreed to the warning.

C-D.evidence: D raised C's laundry (T15) and asked what works for C (T23), and offered once a week (T21). C has not answered, and the laundry problem remains unresolved.
